npcs.speed: 30 ft., fly 30 ft. (hover), swim 40 ft. (ring of swimming)

features.name: Deflection
features.description: Galsariad warps gravity around himself to magically deflect incoming attacks. While Galsariad is wearing no armor and not incapacitated, his AC includes his Intelligence modifier.

features.name: Fey Ancestry
features.description: Galsariad has advantage on saving throws against being charmed, and magic can't put him to sleep.

features.name: Special Equipment
features.description: Galsariad wears a ring of swimming and carries a ruidium dagger (see appendix B). lfhe rolls a 1 on an attack roll made with the dagger, he must succeed on a DC 20 Charisma saving throw or gain 1 level of exhaustion.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Galsariad makes one Drain Potential attack and one Ruidium Dagger attack.

actions.name: Drain Potential
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Spell Attack: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 120 ft., one creature. Hit: 22 (4dl0) necrotic damage, and Galsariad gains 10 temporary hit points.

actions.name: Ruidium Dagger
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 4 (1 d4 + 2) piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) psychic damage.

actions.name: Gravity Rend (Recharge 5-6)
actions.description: Galsariad causes a rippling wave of magical gravity to fill a 30-foot-radius sphere centered on a point he can see within 100 feet of himself. Each creature of Galsariad's choice in that area must make a DC 16 Strength saving throw. On a failed saving throw, the creature takes 42 (12d6) force damage and is restrained for 1 minute. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage and isn't restrained. A restrained creature can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description: Galsariad casts one of the following spells, using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 16): At will: mage hand 1/day each: longstrider, scrying (as an action), slow, telekinesis, water breathing

npcs.description: Galsariad Ardyth is a drow elf wizard.

traps.name: The Box's Riddle (Electric Shock Trap)
traps.trigger: Inserting the incorrect key or trying to pick the lock

detection.detail: Recognizing the shape of the dragon lock or the box's aquatic decorations as indicative of a bronze dragon; if a character saw someone get shocked by lightning after an incorrect guess, the DC for this check is reduced to 11.

disarm.detail: Inserting the correct bronze key opens the lock without triggering the trap.

traps.effect: The lock emits an electric shock.
traps.area: The lock itself
traps.description: A locked wooden box with a dragon-shaped lock that shocks those who insert the wrong key or try to pick it.

traps.name: Ghostgrass Patch
traps.trigger: A creature tries to swim past the ghostgrass

detection.detail: The pale plants blocking the exit to the cavern are ghostgrass, a carnivorous variety of sea grass.

disarm.detail: A creature can use an action to try to free itself or another creature within its reach from the ghostgrass, doing so with a successful DC 12 Strength (Athletics) check.

traps.effect: A creature that tries to swim past the ghostgrass must succeed on a DC 12 Dexterity saving throw or take 3 (1d6) necrotic damage and be restrained. A restrained creature takes the damage again at the start of each of its turns until it escapes.
traps.area: A thick patch of bone-white sea grass blocking the exit to the cavern
traps.description: A carnivorous variety of sea grass that restrains and damages creatures that fail a Dexterity save.

traps.name: Landslide
traps.trigger: As you swim into this area, ripples course through the water as more rocky debris begins to slide toward you.

detection.detail: One side of the chamber is covered in the crumbled and muddy remains of a landslide.

traps.effect: Each character must make a DC 14 Dexterity saving throw, taking 10 (3d6) bludgeoning damage from the landslide on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
traps.area: One side of the chamber covered in crumbled and muddy remains of a landslide
traps.description: A landslide of rocky debris that damages characters who fail a Dexterity save.

traps.name: Sacrifice Engine
traps.trigger: A creature is in the pit while the blades are spinning

detection.detail: The pit is 30 feet deep and lined with rows of silver blades; a lever near the edge can be pulled to spin the blades.

disarm.detail: Pulling the lever near the edge of the pit stops the blades from spinning.

traps.effect: A creature in the pit while the blades are spinning takes 44 (8d10) slashing damage at the start of each of its turns.
traps.area: 30-foot-deep pit
traps.description: A 30-foot-deep pit lined with rows of silver blades that can be made to spin by pulling a lever near the edge.

traps.name: Vrock Corpse Spore Eruption
traps.trigger: A failed DC 15 Wisdom (Survival) check to extract the contents of the vrock's stomach.

detection.detail: To extract the contents of the vrock's stomach, a character must first cleave through the vrock's hide.

disarm.detail: No disarm method described; avoid triggering by succeeding on the Survival check.

traps.effect: An eruption of spores from the vrock's corpse that fill a 10-foot-radius sphere centered on the corpse. All creatures in that area must succeed on a DC 14 Constitution saving throw or become poisoned. A creature poisoned in this way takes 5 (1d10) poison damage at the start of each of its turns. It can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.
traps.area: 10-foot-radius sphere centered on the corpse
traps.description: A failed attempt to cut open a dead vrock's stomach causes a spore eruption.

traps.name: Bladed Corridor
traps.trigger: Whenever one or more creatures are in the hall, the floor tilts to one side and then the other so that creatures stumble into the blades.

detection.detail: Characters who have a passive Wisdom (Perception) score of 12 or higher notice a phrase written in Undercommon on the floor between the two statues.

disarm.detail: If the crystal canister is destroyed, the characters have no way to disable the hall's trap.

traps.effect: A creature that moves into the corridor or starts its turn there must make a DC 20 Dexterity saving throw, taking 17 (5d6) slashing damage on a failed saving throw, or half as much damage on a successful one.
traps.area: The corridor north of the statues
traps.description: A corridor with twitching silver blades protruding from its walls; the floor tilts to make creatures stumble into the blades.

traps.name: Stained-Glass Mosaic Trap
traps.trigger: A creature presses an incorrect symbol on the mosaic

detection.detail: A character who succeeds on a DC 11 Intelligence (Religion) check recognizes these as the symbols of evil gods.

disarm.method: Pressing the correct four symbols in order
disarm.detail: If four of the symbols are pressed in the correct order, as noted in the Symbol Sequence table, a door opens at the base of the wall.

traps.effect: A creature that presses an incorrect symbol must make a DC 16 Wisdom saving throw, taking 28 (8d6) psychic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
traps.area: The stained-glass mosaic
traps.description: A 10-foot-wide section of wall at the north end of the basilica resembles a tall, stained-glass window. Its imagery changes constantly, but nine symbols remain static. If four of the symbols are pressed in the correct order, a door opens. Pressing an incorrect symbol deals psychic damage.

traps.name: Chains of Darkness Trap
traps.trigger: A creature falls prone in the hall (area R10)

detection.detail: A creature that enters this hall immediately feels weighed down and senses a terrible dread. The creature must make a DC 14 Wisdom saving throw.

disarm.detail: Any creature that is not grappled by the chains can use an action to try to free a chained creature within reach, doing so with a successful DC 15 Strength (Athletics) check.

traps.effect: The creature must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or be grappled by the chains (escape DC 15). Until it escapes, the creature takes 5 (1d10) psychic damage at the start of each of its turns. Whatever the result of the check, the creature making the attempt takes 11 (2d10) psychic damage.
traps.damage: 5 (1d10) per turn while grappled; 11 (2d10) to the rescuer
traps.area: The hall (area R10)
traps.description: When a creature falls prone in this hall, the chains on the floor slither toward it, and the figures carved in the walls drone in low voices. The creature must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or be grappled by the chains, taking psychic damage each turn.

traps.name: Abyssal Rift
traps.trigger: When a creature passes through the gaping mouth of the stone-carved face of Gruumsh in area R15

detection.detail: The rift is visible as a 10-foot-wide, 20-foot-long orifice filled with impenetrable darkness. Horrible shrieks emanate from it.

disarm.detail: The rift closes after 1 minute automatically. No disarm method is given.

traps.effect: A creature that enters the rift from this side is magically transported, along with anything it is wearing or carrying, to the Abyss. The creature emerges from a similar rift located inside a colossal cyclone of poisonous gas. A creature caught in the cyclone is trapped there and takes 14 (4d6) poison damage at the start of each of its turns. A creature that has a flying speed can escape the cyclone by flying into the rift; a creature without a flying speed can use an action to try to harness the winds of the cyclone, propelling itself through the rift with a successful DC 19 Dexterity (Acrobatics) check.
traps.area: 10-foot-wide, 20-foot-long orifice; cyclone is colossal
traps.description: A planar rift that opens in the floor on the east side of the chasm when a creature passes through the carving of Gruumsh's face. It is a gateway to the Abyss.

traps.name: Vault Trap
traps.trigger: If the vault is opened by any means other than using the master key, the vault's magical trap is triggered.

detection.detail: A character who examines the vault and succeeds on a successful DC 20 Intelligence (Investigation) check finds a thin keyhole near its base.

disarm.detail: The trap can't be disarmed, but successfully casting dispel magic (DC 15) on the lock before an attempt is made to open it suppresses the trap for 1 minute, allowing the lock to be manipulated without negative consequences.

traps.effect: Each creature within 5 feet of the vault must make a DC 16 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed saving throw, a creature takes 36 (8d8) psychic damage and is stunned for 1 minute. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage and isn't stunned.
traps.area: Each creature within 5 feet of the vault
traps.description: A magical trap on the casino's coin vault that triggers if opened without the master key.

traps.name: Vault Door Energy Blast Trap
traps.trigger: Forcing the vault door open (DC 21 Strength (Athletics) check)

detection.detail: A character who searches the basement and succeeds on a DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check notices the faint outline of a circular stone door in the wall next to a bookcase that is bolted to the floor.

disarm.detail: This trap can't be disarmed.

traps.effect: A loud, concussive blast of energy fills a 15-foot cube immediately outside the vault. Any creature in the cube must make a DC 18 Constitution saving throw, taking 33 (6d10) thunder damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
traps.area: 15-foot cube immediately outside the vault
traps.description: A magical trap that releases a concussive blast of energy when the vault door is forced open.

traps.name: Trapdoor (disguised as symbol of Corellon)
traps.trigger: A character who searches the tower ruins and succeeds on a DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation) check discovers a large symbol of Corellon inscribed on the floor, mostly hidden under sand and debris. Closer examination discloses a 5-foot-diameter, circular stone trapdoor disguised as part of the symbol.

detection.detail: A character who searches the tower ruins and succeeds on a DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation) check discovers a large symbol of Corellon inscribed on the floor, mostly hidden under sand and debris. Closer examination discloses a 5-foot-diameter, circular stone trapdoor disguised as part of the symbol.

disarm.detail: The trapdoor is closed and stuck. A character can use an action to try to pry it up by using a crowbar or similar tool.

traps.effect: The trapdoor is closed and stuck. A character can use an action to try to pry it up by using a crowbar or similar tool.
traps.area: 5-foot-diameter circular stone trapdoor
traps.description: A stone trapdoor disguised as part of a symbol of Corellon, stuck and requiring effort to open.

traps.name: Burst of Radiance Trap
traps.trigger: A creature enters the armory without first saying a prayer to Corellon.

detection.detail: A character who searches the opening for traps and succeeds on a DC 17 Intelligence (Investigation) check spots a tiny glyph inscribed along the edge of the opening, in a location that's not visible while the trapdoor is closed.

disarm.method: dispel magic (DC 17) or defaced using mason's tools or similar equipment
disarm.detail: If this glyph is dispelled with a successful casting of dispel magic (DC 17) or defaced using mason's tools or similar equipment, the following trap ceases to function.

traps.effect: A burst of radiance flares from the chamber. Each creature in the armory and within 15 feet of the trapdoor must make a DC 18 Constitution saving throw, taking 33 (6d10) radiant damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. This trap can be triggered only once.
traps.area: The armory and within 15 feet of the trapdoor
traps.description: A magical trap that triggers a burst of radiant damage when a creature enters the armory without praying to Corellon.

traps.name: Secret Door (Netherdeep)
traps.trigger: Any creature within 10 feet of a secret door that deals damage to it

detection.detail: A character who spends at least 10 minutes searching an area for secret doors can make a DC 20 Intelligence (Investigation) check at the end of that search. If the check succeeds and there's a secret door to be found, the character finds it.

disarm.detail: Secret doors in the Netherdeep are unlocked unless otherwise noted, and they open easily despite their great weight.

traps.effect: Any creature within 10 feet of a secret door that deals damage to it must make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw, taking 22 (4d10) psychic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
traps.area: 10-foot radius around the secret door
traps.description: A secret door made of ruidium-veined stone that deals psychic damage to creatures that damage it.

traps.name: Boiling Water (Vents of Fury)
traps.trigger: If the bloodfin is killed, the vents in the floor flare with bright red light and spew forth a flood of boiling-hot water.

detection.detail: Characters who have a passive Wisdom (Perception) score of 17 or higher notice something more: At the far end of the thirty-foot-high cavern, a monstrous fish with a red-streaked body chases a school of much smaller fish.

disarm.detail: No disarm method described.

traps.effect: Any creature that starts its turn in the boiling-hot water must make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw, taking 21 (6d6) fire damage on a failed saving throw, or half as much damage on a successful one. The scalding heat lasts for 1 hour, after which the vents return to their normal illumination and the water temperature in the cavern again becomes bearably warm.
traps.area: The entire cavern (area N10)
traps.description: The bubbling columns of water rising from the vents are hot, but not hot enough to damage creatures that enter them. If the bloodfin is killed, the vents spew boiling-hot water.

traps.name: Ruidium Spines (Current Trap)
traps.trigger: If the characters kill the light devourer, the current intensifies for 1 hour. Until the current returns to normal, any creature that starts its turn in this chamber must succeed on a DC 14 Strength saving throw or be thrust against a wall by the current and skewered by ruidium spines.

detection.detail: The walls are lined with ruidium spines, visible to any creature entering the chamber.

disarm.detail: No disarm method described; the trap is triggered by killing the light devourer.

traps.effect: The creature takes 5 (1d10) piercing damage from the spines and must succeed on a DC 20 Charisma saving throw or gain 1 level of exhaustion. If the creature is not already suffering from ruidium corruption, it becomes corrupted when it fails the saving throw.
traps.area: Area N11 (Frothing Hollow)
traps.description: A current threatens to pull creatures into this chamber, the walls of which are lined with ruidium spines. The Apotheon's ragged breathing is audible. Thermal vents in the floor give off swirling bubbles, dim light, and warmth.

traps.name: Scalding Pit (Boiling Water)
traps.trigger: If either the ruidium greatsword or the ruidium shield is removed from its resting place, the vents in the floor flare with bright red light and spew forth a flood of boiling-hot water

detection.detail: The vents in the floor are visible, but the trap is triggered by removing the items.

disarm.detail: The trap cannot be disarmed; it lasts for 1 hour after triggering.

traps.effect: Any creature that starts its turn in the boiling water must make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw, taking 21 (6d6) fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. The scalding heat lasts for 1 hour, after which the vents return to their normal illumination and the water temperature changes from boiling hot to bearably warm.
traps.area: The water in the chamber up to a height of 30 feet
traps.description: Natural vents spew red light and jets of bubbling water. Removing the ruidium items triggers a flood of boiling-hot water.

traps.name: Ruidium Tendrils (Apotheon's Fury)
traps.trigger: When all three serpentmaws in area N13 are dead, dozens of tendrils of ruidium emerge from the statues in the cavern.

detection.detail: The tendrils emerge automatically after the serpentmaws are killed.

disarm.detail: The tendrils persist for 1 minute, after which they recede back into the statues.

traps.effect: Any creature that enters the cavern or starts its turn there must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or be grappled by a tendril (escape DC 15). While grappled in this way, a creature is also restrained. No more than one tendril can grapple a single creature. Each tendril is an Ooze that has AC 15; 10 hit points; immunity to all damage except slashing; Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution scores of 20; and Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores of 1. A tendril reduced to 0 hit points disintegrates in a crimson haze. On initiative count 0, each creature grappled by a tendril takes 3 (1d6) piercing damage and 3 (1d6) psychic damage as it is flung against one of the cavern's ruidium spikes. The creature remains grappled after taking this damage; in addition, it must succeed on a DC 20 Charisma saving throw or gain 1 level of exhaustion. If the creature is not already suffering from ruidium corruption, it becomes corrupted when it fails the saving throw.
traps.area: The cavern (area N13)
traps.description: When the serpentmaws are killed, ruidium tendrils emerge from statues, grappling and flinging creatures against spikes.

traps.name: East Door Trap
traps.trigger: The first time the door is touched

detection.detail: The door gives off a flash of crimson light when touched.

disarm.detail: A character can use an action to try to pick the lock with thieves' tools, doing so with a successful DC 22 Dexterity check. A knock spell or similar magic also opens the door.

traps.effect: Any creature within 10 feet of the door when this happens must succeed on a DC 18 Strength saving throw or be pushed 20 feet away from the door- and into the death embrace's tentacles, if that creature is still alive and present.
traps.area: 10 feet of the door
traps.description: A sturdy cellar door with a built-in lock that triggers a crimson flash and pushes creatures away when first touched.

traps.name: The Box's Riddle Lock
traps.trigger: A character inserts an incorrect key into the lock or tries to pick the lock.

detection.detail: A character who succeeds on a DC 13 Intelligence (Arcana or History) check recognizes the shape of the dragon lock or the box's aquatic decorations as indicative of a bronze dragon; if a character saw someone get shocked by lightning after an incorrect guess, the DC for this check is reduced to 11. A character can make a DC 10 Intelligence check to recognize that the metallic hues of the keys and the first two lines of the riddle are talking about not just metals but also types of metallic dragons.

disarm.detail: The correct key (the bronze key) opens the lock without triggering the trap. Inserting the incorrect key or trying to pick the lock triggers the shock.

traps.effect: The lock emits an electric shock.
traps.area: The creature inserting the incorrect key or picking the lock
traps.description: A locked wooden box with four metal keys (bronze, copper, silver, gold). The lock is shaped like a dragon with a fluted crest, and the box edges are decorated with engravings of pearls and shells. The bronze key opens the lock; incorrect keys or lockpicking triggers an electric shock.
traps.source: Critical Role: Call of the Netherdeep p.7

traps.name: Bottle 2 (Blight Brew)
traps.trigger: A character sips from this bottle.

detection.detail: The bottle is green and filled with blight brew.

disarm.detail: Not applicable; the bottle is simply avoided or the correct bottle is chosen.

traps.effect: The character becomes poisoned for 1 minute, spending the time retching.
traps.area: The creature sipping from the bottle
traps.description: Bottle 2 of the Bottles' Riddle is a green bottle filled with blight brew. Sipping from it requires a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or the character becomes poisoned for 1 minute, retching.
traps.source: Critical Role: Call of the Netherdeep p.7

traps.name: Bottle 4 (Spicy Pepper Oil)
traps.trigger: A character sips from this bottle.

detection.detail: The bottle is white and filled with overwhelmingly spicy pepper oil.

disarm.detail: Not applicable; the bottle is simply avoided or the correct bottle is chosen.

traps.effect: The character takes 1 fire damage from the spice.
traps.area: The creature sipping from the bottle
traps.description: Bottle 4 of the Bottles' Riddle is a white bottle filled with overwhelmingly spicy pepper oil. Sipping from it requires a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or the character takes 1 fire damage from the spice.
traps.source: Critical Role: Call of the Netherdeep p.7

traps.name: Stained-Glass Mosaic
traps.trigger: A creature presses an incorrect symbol on the stained-glass mosaic.

detection.detail: A character who succeeds on a DC 11 Intelligence (Religion) check recognizes the nine symbols as the symbols of evil gods.

disarm.detail: The mosaic can be bypassed by pressing four symbols in the correct order (Spider, Bleeding Eye, Jagged Spiral, Trio of Arms), or by breaking through it with a successful DC 12 Strength check or by destroying it.

traps.effect: A creature that presses an incorrect symbol must make a DC 16 Wisdom saving throw, taking 28 (8d6) psychic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. Destroying the mosaic causes the flame creatures in the hall to attack. Moreover, each creature in the hall when the mosaic breaks must make a DC 20 Wisdom saving throw unless it is a Construct, a Fiend, or an Undead. On a failed save, the creature is cursed and can't regain hit points until the effect on that creature is ended by a remove curse spell or similar magic. If destroyed, the stained-glass window repairs itself after 1 hour.
traps.area: The stained-glass mosaic is a 10-foot-wide section of wall at the north end of the basilica.
traps.description: A stained-glass mosaic depicting a maelstrom of color with nine symbols of evil gods. Pressing the correct sequence of four symbols opens a door; pressing an incorrect symbol triggers psychic damage.

traps.name: Chains of Darkness
traps.trigger: A creature falls prone in the hall of area R10.

detection.detail: The chains on the floor slither toward the creature when it falls prone.

disarm.detail: Any creature that is not grappled by the chains can use an action to try to free a chained creature within reach, doing so with a successful DC 15 Strength (Athletics) check. Whatever the result of the check, the creature making the attempt takes 11 (2d10) psychic damage.

traps.effect: The creature must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or be grappled by the chains (escape DC 15). Until it escapes, the creature takes 5 (1d10) psychic damage at the start of each of its turns.
traps.area: The hall of area R10, which is covered by a nest of black chains.
traps.description: When a creature falls prone in this hall, the chains on the floor slither toward it and attempt to grapple it, dealing psychic damage each turn.

traps.name: Wailing Statue
traps.trigger: Any creature within 30 feet of the statue that can hear the wailing sound coming from it

detection.detail: A detect magic spell reveals an aura of abjuration magic emanating from the iron doors in the statue's chest. Similar auras are apparent in the palms of the stone arms that are within the spell's range.

disarm.detail: The curse can be ended by a remove curse spell or similar magic, or by entering area R16.

traps.effect: Any creature within 30 feet of the statue that can hear the wailing sound coming from it must make a successful DC 16 Charisma saving throw or become cursed by Torog's hunger. A creature that succeeds on this saving throw is immune to the effect of the wailing statue for 24 hours. The curse has the following effects on a creature: • At the start of each of its turns, the creature must make a DC 16 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the creature must use its action to harm another creature it can see, using a spell or an attack that deals the greatest amount of damage. • While the creature has fewer than half its hit points, its successful weapon attacks deal an extra 3 (1d6) psychic damage. The creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. Otherwise, the curse of Torog remains in effect on the creature until ended by a remove curse spell or similar magic, or until the creature enters area R16.
traps.area: 30-foot radius around the statue
traps.description: A statue of a tortured man that emits a hideous wailing noise, cursing those who hear it with Torog's hunger.

traps.name: Arms of Torog Pustules
traps.trigger: Attacking or destroying the pustules on the palms of the stone arms

detection.detail: Characters who have a passive Wisdom (Perception) score of 13 or higher notice that each one of the arms bears a throbbing, purple-black pustule on its palm.

disarm.detail: Destroying all three pustules lights up the entire triangle and unlocks the doors embedded in the statue's chest. If the pustules are all destroyed, they re-form after 1 hour, at which point the doors close and become locked again unless they are held open or are opened from the inside.

traps.effect: Each pustule has AC 17, 25 hit points, and immunity to poison and psychic damage. When a pustule is reduced to 0 hit points, it is destroyed, and one side of the triangle engraved on the floor begins to glow white. Destroying all three pustules lights up the entire triangle and unlocks the doors embedded in the statue's chest.
traps.area: Three stone arms at the points of a 40-foot triangle around the statue
traps.description: Three stone arms jut up from the floor, each with a throbbing purple-black pustule on its palm. Destroying all three unlocks the iron doors in the statue's chest.

traps.name: South Hallway Stone Slab
traps.trigger: When one or more characters enter the hallway to the south

detection.detail: The grinding noise is heard automatically when entering the hallway.

disarm.detail: Defeating the fiendish ores in area R14 or using a knock spell or similar magic causes the slab to sink back into the floor; it can't be moved or breached otherwise.

traps.effect: A loud grinding noise is heard as a stone slab rises from the floor to block the entrance to area R14. This slab has no handle or keyhole.
traps.area: Entrance to area R14
traps.description: A stone slab rises to block the southern hallway, sealing off area R14 until the fiendish ores are defeated or a knock spell is used.

traps.name: Lightless Labyrinth
traps.trigger: Entering the labyrinth and choosing paths

detection.detail: A character who makes a successful DC 14 Intelligence (Religion) check recalls one of Torog's commandments: "Seek and exalt places where no light touches." A character can guess that the darkened passages are related by making a successful DC 10 Wisdom (Insight) check.

disarm.detail: Always take the fork shrouded in darkness. After choosing three paths, if they chose the darkened path all three times, they emerge at the opposite side from where they entered.

traps.effect: When the characters enter the labyrinth, they're faced with a choice of three paths: one lit by violet continual flame spells, one by red continual flame spells, and one shrouded in impenetrable magical darkness. Following any of the paths leads them to another three-way fork with the same choices available, and then another. If they chose any of the illuminated paths, they emerge at the same place where they entered, and each character must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or gain 1 level of exhaustion as the endlessly zigzagging pathways drain their resolve.
traps.area: Network of 5-foot-wide, 10-foot-high tunnels
traps.description: A zigzagging labyrinth with three paths at each fork: violet-lit, red-lit, and magical darkness. Taking the dark path leads to the exit; taking lit paths causes exhaustion.

traps.name: Blood Font of the Ruiner
traps.trigger: The ores pray to Gruumsh on their first turn in combat, activating the blood font

detection.detail: The pool of blood is visible in the center of the chamber.

disarm.detail: Killing both ores or forcing open either exit causes the boiling blood to drain out of the room through holes that open in the floor, lowering the blood's depth by 5 feet per round.

traps.effect: Stone slabs rise from the floor to block the north and south exits (unless both slabs were already closed). A knock spell or similar magic can force a slab to sink back into the floor. When both exits are sealed after the ores pray to Gruumsh, the pool of blood begins to boil and overflow. The boiling blood starts to flood the room, rising at a rate of 5 feet per minute to a maximum depth of 45 feet. A creature that ends its turn in the boiling blood takes 7 (2d6) fire damage.
traps.area: Entire chamber, flooding up to 45 feet deep
traps.description: A circular pool of blood that, when activated by the ores' prayer to Gruumsh, seals the exits and floods the room with boiling blood.

traps.name: Vault Door Concussive Blast
traps.trigger: A character forcibly pries open the vault door with a successful DC 21 Strength (Athletics) check.

detection.detail: This trap can't be disarmed.

disarm.detail: This trap can't be disarmed.

traps.effect: Forcing the vault open produces a loud, concussive blast of energy that fills a 15-foot cube immediately outside the vault.
traps.area: 15-foot cube immediately outside the vault
traps.description: A magical trap that triggers when the vault door is forcibly pried open, releasing a concussive blast of thunder damage.

traps.name: Lockbox Poison Gas Trap
traps.trigger: Forcing open the metal lockbox (prying it open with a successful DC 16 Strength (Athletics) check) causes poison gas to spray outward.

detection.detail: A character who makes a successful DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation) check locates the metal lockbox stowed underneath an upside-down crate in a corner of the room.

disarm.detail: The lockbox can be opened safely by a character who makes a successful DC 21 Dexterity check using thieves' tools.

traps.effect: Poison gas sprays outward, and the character who opened it must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or take 22 (4d10) poison damage and be poisoned for 1 hour.
traps.area: The character who opened the box
traps.description: A metal lockbox hidden under an upside-down crate sprays poison gas when forced open.

traps.name: Secret Armory Glyph Trap
traps.trigger: If a creature enters the armory without first saying a prayer to Corellon

detection.detail: A character who searches the opening for traps and succeeds on a DC 17 Intelligence (Investigation) check spots a tiny glyph inscribed along the edge of the opening, in a location that's not visible while the trapdoor is closed.

disarm.detail: If this glyph is dispelled with a successful casting of dispel magic (DC 17) or defaced using mason's tools or similar equipment, the following trap ceases to function.

traps.effect: a burst of radiance flares from the chamber. Each creature in the armory and within 15 feet of the trapdoor must make a DC 18 Constitution saving throw, taking 33 (6d10) radiant damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. This trap can be triggered only once.
traps.area: Each creature in the armory and within 15 feet of the trapdoor
traps.description: A magical glyph trap in a secret armory that triggers a burst of radiant damage if a creature enters without praying to Corellon.
traps.source: Critical Role: Call of the Netherdeep p.Chapter 5

traps.name: Scalding Pit Boiling Water
traps.trigger: Removing either the ruidium greatsword or the ruidium shield from its resting place causes the vents in the floor to flare with bright red light and spew forth a flood of boiling-hot water, drastically raising the temperature of the water in the chamber to a height of 30 feet.

detection.detail: No detection check specified; the trap is triggered by removing the items.

disarm.detail: No disarm method specified; the scalding heat lasts for 1 hour, after which the vents return to normal.

traps.effect: Any creature that starts its turn in the boiling water must make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw, taking 21 (6d6) fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. The scalding heat lasts for 1 hour.
traps.area: The water in the chamber up to a height of 30 feet.
traps.description: Removing either ruidium item from its vent triggers a flood of boiling-hot water in the Scalding Pit chamber.
traps.source: Critical Role: Call of the Netherdeep p. (N12)

traps.name: Ruidium Tendrils
traps.trigger: When all three serpentmaws in area N13 are dead, dozens of tendrils of ruidium emerge from the statues in the cavern.

detection.detail: No detection check specified; tendrils appear automatically after the serpentmaws are killed.

disarm.detail: Each tendril can be destroyed; it is an Ooze with AC 15, 10 hit points, immunity to all damage except slashing, Strength/Dexterity/Constitution 20, Intelligence/Wisdom/Charisma 1. A tendril reduced to 0 hit points disintegrates.

traps.effect: Any creature that enters the cavern or starts its turn there must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or be grappled by a tendril (escape DC 15). While grappled, the creature is also restrained. On initiative count 0, each creature grappled by a tendril takes 3 (1d6) piercing damage and 3 (1d6) psychic damage as it is flung against a ruidium spike. The creature remains grappled and must succeed on a DC 20 Charisma saving throw or gain 1 level of exhaustion. If not already suffering from ruidium corruption, it becomes corrupted when it fails the saving throw.
traps.area: The entire cavern of area N13.
traps.description: After the serpentmaws are slain, ruidium tendrils emerge from statues and grapple creatures in the cavern.
traps.source: Critical Role: Call of the Netherdeep p. (N13)
